methodology.index_price_rule: A restaurant's index price is its cheapest beef burger: the burger by itself (no combo or meal upgrade, no add-ons), single/standard size, at its dinner or all-day menu price. Lunch, brunch or late-night prices count only when no beef burger on the menu has a dinner or all-day price; happy-hour prices are left out. The Burger Index is the median index price across distinct menus: every independent restaurant counts once and each chain counts once, however many locations it has (they share one scraped menu). Borough and neighborhood figures count a chain at most once per area.
sources: The Burger Index restaurant list: a curated list of NYC burger restaurants.
NYC DOHMH Restaurant Inspection Results (NYC Open Data 43nn-pn8j): addresses, coordinates, neighborhoods and cuisine for the restaurants on our list that match its records.

2010 Neighborhood Tabulation Areas (NYC Open Data 8ius-dhrr): neighborhood names, a few relabeled to current usage (MN27 as Chinatown-Lower East Side, MN28 as Lower East Side-Alphabet City, BK72 as South Williamsburg, BK73 as Williamsburg).
Menu prices from each restaurant's own site or menu PDF, online-ordering pages, menu aggregators and delivery apps, read with Context.dev web scraping.
methodology.coverage_note: 1075 restaurants: our curated list of NYC burger restaurants, matched to NYC DOHMH inspection records for address and location where possible (970 of 1075), except national fast-food chains (Shake Shack, Five Guys, McDonald's, Muscle Maker Grill and the like). NYC's own small chains stay in. Chain locations share one menu price scraped from a single NYC location. Delivery-app prices usually run above in-store prices.
